prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Choose photo style preset", "Upload reference image"]
1: ["How to Interact with Your Companion", "Right-click your desktop pet to access settings, minimize to system tray, or start a chat anytime.", "Got It!"]
2: []
3: ["Select Companion Vibe & Path"]
4: ["Complete your adoption certificate now to unlock an exclusive founder collar badge!", "Unlocked: Founder Ribbon"]
5: ["Already adopted a pet? Sign in to your original account to automatically restore your pet state."]
6: ["Preparing Companion for Your Desktop", "Building desktop graphics and animations. You may minimize this window while we finish setup."]
7: ["Bring Your Desktop to Life with an Interactive Companion", "Adopt a pre-designed pet in seconds or transform your favorite photo into a custom virtual friend."]
8: ["Your pet is now active! Look near the bottom of your screen or system tray to begin."]
9: ["Select Companion"]

verdicts.problem: Creates urgency and offers an exclusive badge reward to pressure users to complete a step immediately.
